title: The Cerebral Lobes
subtitle: Useful landmarks, not sealed compartments
learningObjectives: Use frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes as anatomical orientation landmarks.
Relate lobe-level specialisation to distributed network function.
Explain why lesion side, extent and connectivity matter more than a lobe label alone.

sections.explainSimply: The cortex is divided into lobes that help us describe where things happen. The borders are landmarks, not walls.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Frontal systems support executive control and action; parietal systems integrate sensory-spatial information; temporal systems support audition, memory and meaning; occipital cortex processes vision.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Each lobe contains multiple cytoarchitectonic and functional areas with extensive intra- and inter-lobar connectivity. Clinical effects depend on lesion side, extent, network position and premorbid organisation.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Suburbs in one city: each has a recognisable character, but roads and services cross every boundary.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Lobe-based summaries are useful for formulation but too coarse for definitive localisation or diagnosis.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Injury may produce executive dysfunction, neglect, aphasia, agnosia or visual field deficits depending on network involvement.
sections.clinicalPearl: Use lobes to orient yourself; use networks and behaviour to reason clinically.
sections.practicalExample: A right parietal lesion may disrupt spatial attention, but the severity and pattern depend on which cortical regions and connecting white-matter pathways are affected.
sections.limitationsCautions: Lobe-based localisation is deliberately coarse. Avoid statements such as “the frontal lobe controls personality” or “the temporal lobe is the memory centre.”

quizBank.question: Which lobe is most directly associated with primary visual processing?
quizBank.explanation: Primary visual cortex is located in the occipital lobe.

reviewPrompts.prompt: Explain the cerebral lobes in clinically useful terms.
reviewPrompts.answer: Frontal systems support executive control and action; parietal systems integrate sensory-spatial information; temporal systems support audition, memory and meaning; occipital cortex processes vision.
